reports.say_back: Through an outsider's first ten minutes: it is an index, not an account. There is a diagram of eleven abstract slots ("a stock", "a rule", "a reading") joined by labelled arrows, each with four tiny squares, mostly empty. Below it are tables of counts: laws per tie, predictions per verdict, bridges held or failed. The detail pages give theorem paraphrases like "Where two drawers have no floor, in every perfect profile every drawer leaves exactly its floor at every step before the horizon". I learned no claim about how anything forms, lasts, changes or ends. Nothing new is possible for me: I cannot follow a commons, a reward or a market through the picture and see what happens to it. I would tell a friend: "It's a catalogue of a large private library of Lean theorems, filed by an AI under a home-made schema, plus a scorecard of its own experiments. The ideas may be in there, but this page doesn't say them." The word "alignment" never appears on the page.
reports.why_not_good_enough: Ren asked for a map of how things become, something that "can show its topology, can show the relationship between different things". He wanted it holistic and layered like Wikipedia, so that a person "can see the value of it". What was built is a schema of the filing system: a type diagram of argument slots, with the laws sorted under pairs of slots and counted. It answers "where is a law about X stored, and how many are there", not "what happens to X". The picture disowns being a map in its own caption: "an arrow is not a route", "A tie gathers laws of separate models". A course can't be traced on it: capture forming, a loss growing beyond what a rule reads, a lock, an exit. The dynamics, which are the actual places where things happen, are hidden in a dropdown ("choose one of 160"). The page's energy goes into epistemic bookkeeping: frozen predictions, bridges, "if met / not checked", 11-column count tables. That is the AI's concern with not overclaiming, not the reader's question. Even on its own terms the four questions come out mostly blank: 19 of 19 drawn ties have no general law for "changes". The account's real content is selection reaching only what couples in, the drain beyond it, the lock and the lake. It lives in ONE-PAGE and never surfaces here. So the map is a precise index sitting in front of the account, not a map of it.

keep: The separation of reasoning from situation is real and worth keeping: the 'if met / then seen' table in THE-MAP.md 'Where reasoning has met a case' (26 agree, 0 met-but-not-seen, 32 failed mostly at the bridge) is the one place where an outsider sees the theory being risked against data.

Each case's one-line summary in its own words (screenshots 4-5, right column, e.g. EM1 'Wherever the others outran the regrowth (9,026 windows) the patch stayed empty, as the law says') is concrete and readable, and is the best material on the page.

The dynamic panel's one-sentence statement with its roles in its own model's words (screenshot 7, 'A rule set from the share of what it favours, and read in a way formed from that share, stays locked while a loss it never reads grows without bound') is the right grain for a place on a map.

reports.a_good_one_would: In the first minute it would let me watch a course: something drawing on what sustains it, a selection that reads only part of what it affects, the favoured share rising, the rule locking, an unread loss growing, and the points where it can still be left or can no longer be. Each step would be stated plainly, with its everyday names (commons, Goodhart, lock-in, a reward model) and where AI alignment sits on it. I could pick a situation I know and follow its arrows to what tends to happen next and what would change that. Each place would open into a short, Wikipedia-like article: the claim, one picture, one case such as the lake, and how far it is shown. Proofs, counts and test bookkeeping would sit one layer down, reachable but not the face.
reports.against_ren: Mostly nothing. One point in the map's favour: Ren's own aim, "separate logic and situation", partly produced the bookkeeping face. The if/then verdict table is that aim carried out faithfully, and it is the most credible thing on the page. The fault is putting that separation forward as the content, not having it at all. A second, smaller point: his "a map, not a set of maps" pushed toward one abstract schema general enough to hold every model. Generality at that level is exactly what empties the picture of trajectories. One map can still have regions and routes, and here "one" was read as "one type diagram".

reports.say_back: Someone who comes with a problem learns that the theory has a grammar: eleven kinds of role (a stock, the drawers, a rule, its readers...), the ties between them, four squares on each tie, and counts. They do not learn where their problem is or what the theory says about it. The fisher is sent to "the drawers · draws on · a stock", a tie that 80 dynamics share. There they get one law per grammatical slot, for example "in every perfect profile every drawer leaves exactly its floor... InTurn.Perfect; and 2 more". Nothing on the page says what decides collapse against keeping. The person with a reward problem is sent to "a rule · selects and favours", and the first law under "lasts" there is a market share rising. The person asking about the meta-attractor finds no such word on the landing page. Humans and AI appear nowhere. The theory's real answers to all three questions exist, but they are spread across ties and pages, and nothing on the map assembles them for the person who asked.
reports.why_not_good_enough: What was built is an index of the theory's own grammar: roles × ties × {begins, lasts, changes, ends} × forms, with counts in each cell. What was asked for is a map, a thing you find yourself on and then see where you can go from there. The landed map's nodes are kinds of role, and you cannot be "at a stock". Its arrows, it says itself, are "not a route", so it cannot show where anything leads. The two earlier rounds had both of these. Round 1 had places, "a condition something can be in: renewing within what it is given, drawing past it... past the point of no return" (WHOLE-PICTURE.md). Round 2 had questions in the asker's words, "Is something used up that the rule does not count?", and a "Where a case stands: answer the questions for something you know" (DESIGN.md). Ren said yes to both. The foundation round then swapped places and questions for role-kinds, and the landed web.json holds roles, ties, marks, forms and frames, with no places, no situations and no transitions. Meanwhile the atlas holds 103 transitions and 321 exits, which is exactly the "where it leads" a person needs. So the map returns to what WHOLE-PICTURE.md named as the first failure: "nothing to draw but boxes with counts". The relational vocabulary was cleaned up, but the reader still has to do the theory's work.

reports.a_good_one_would: The fisher would start from their own question, or a few plain questions about their situation ('do the boats each count only their own catch?', 'does anything count what the bay needs to regrow?', 'how far ahead do they weigh the catch?'). They would land on a named place, such as 'joint take past renewal, each counting its own', and see in one view what holds them there, which neighbouring places they could move to and what moves them (a floor, coupling each step, counting what is left), and where it ends. Each arrow would say how far it has been seen. Beside it they would see the lake test, what it showed, and where its bridge failed. The reward asker would find 'reads only what couples in -> drains beyond -> rule read from its share locks -> rewarding those who break correction', which is the meta-attractor, drawn as one route. Off every step of it would hang the exits the account proves, and humans and AI would be named as the selectors.
reports.against_ren: Ren's words and the map are partly at odds over the logic/situation split. The landed map does keep laws and cases strictly apart and shows where they have met ('the if was met and the then was not seen (0)'). That honours his clear goal, and the separation should stay. The map is also right not to draw routes the Lean does not join. But it overcorrects. The atlas's transitions and exits are recorded with their declarations, so routes could be drawn with how far each has been seen, rather than refused. Taking 'no person-words' as a reason to drop the asker's language altogether (0 'human', 0 'reward' on the landing page) goes beyond what Ren asked. His complaint was about 人 used for things that are not people, not about naming the people and AI the map is for.

reports.say_back: A reader is told that laws and cases are kept apart and that a case cannot make a proved law wrong. Then they get a 2x2 table of counts whose key cell, "if met, then not seen", reads 0. The conclusion they carry away is that nothing has gone against the account: 26 agreements, no contradictions, and the rest set aside because a condition failed. The picture shows only the reasoning, eleven roles and their ties. Situations appear only as green dots and rings, which count tests and say nothing about what happened in them. To learn what fish stocks, a Q-learner or a gradient-trained policy actually showed, and what that changed in the reasoning, the reader has to leave the map for the test folders. The map stores the meetings of reasoning and data as verdict categories. It does not show them as relationships a reader can follow.
reports.why_not_good_enough: Ren asked for a map that shows how reasoning and actual data relate: where each was right or wrong, and how each moved the other. What was built is a well-kept ledger of those meetings, with each frozen prediction coded by if-state, outcome and failed_at, and then counted. The relationship he asked for has direction and history: a premise found false in the field, the state widened, new laws proved, a thesis rewritten. It also has rivals: something else predicts the same. The ledger cuts that into cells. In the published views it is gone: the history (afterwards_en) appears only in the interactive page, and rival reasoning (rival_en, on 137 of 180 predictions) appears once in CASES.md. The 2x2 frame is borrowed from material implication. It makes "reasoning met data" a question about whether the account was refuted, which is the defend-every-claim stance the new AGENTS.md set aside. The question it should answer is how far each line of reasoning reaches into which situations. A deliberate test of a thesis beyond its law (LA4 asks: does the drain hold short of the optimum?) is filed as "if not met". A situation that taught the theory something (MQ3) is filed as "neither held". The picture holds only the logic, and the situations stay off it.

findings.what: The four corners teach that the account is unrefuted, not how reasoning and data relate; the 0 cell is the headline, and the 26 include predictions that say more than any law.

Across all 66 tests, only 9 predictions follow from a law, had every condition met and were seen. The page never states that figure.

keep: The foundation of laws, cases and bridges kept apart, with each case's 'Taken as' pairing of its own words to roles (CASES.md; cases.json 'things' and 'bridges'), is the right ground for separating logic from situation.

Each frozen prediction in cases.json carries its conditions with how each was assessed (built, measured, argued, not checked) and their state, plus failed_at, rival_en and seen_en. That is the raw material of the relationship Ren asked for.
afterwards_en in cases.json (for example MQ3's chain to MQ4, MQ5, RM2-RM5 and T2) records how a situation changed the reasoning. It should be promoted to the main views.

THE-MAP.md line 119's tally of where failures were placed (the bridge 38, statistical power 13, the measure 10, ...) points the right way: failures put in the joint between reasoning and data, not blamed on either side.
The interactive case view ('each role shows what the case took as that role ... the ties whose laws it met turn green') is the one place a case is laid onto the web, and it is worth building out.
reports.a_good_one_would: Take one test, say MQ3. A reader sees, on one surface, the law in plain words with its premise, the situation in its own words, and the bridge drawn between them, marked where it broke: 'giving read off the level' was false in managed stocks. They see what happened next: the state widened (MQ4, MQ5), new laws were proved (RM2-RM5), the thesis was rewritten (T2). Where something else predicts the same, as policy gradient does for LA4 and known learning theory does for CG3, that rival appears beside it. Situations have places on the map, not only dots, so a reader can start from a situation of their own (an aquifer, a recommender), find the nearest tested cases and the premises to check first, and see how far each line of reasoning has been carried into situations like it: proved, held, failed at a bridge, or untried.
reports.against_ren: In one respect the map is right and should not give way. A Lean-proved law really cannot be refuted by a case, and a meeting of logic and data needs a third thing, the bridge or reading. Ren's wording, "separate logic and situation", is two-sided. What the map gets right is putting failures in that joint (bridge 38, measure 10). The fault is that the joint is shown as categories and counts, and the sentence "a case cannot make a proved law wrong" is presented as a wall. It should be shown as reach: how far each law's premises are known to hold in which situations. Ren's 'even when one is right, the other could be wrong' should also cover logic that is valid but about the wrong model. The map can show that only as a 'thesis' or 'bridge' failure, and it should say so plainly.

reports.say_back: Through this lens a reader comes away with: the theory's laws are written with eleven kinds of noun and about a dozen kinds of verb; most concern a stock or a rule; here is how many laws are filed under each noun-verb-noun under four headings, and how few a test has touched. The reader does not come away with what happens: how a commons runs down, how a rule locks, what follows the lock, when it is too late, what leads out, where the meta-attractor sits, or where a case they know stands. The picture reads as a wiring list of the vocabulary with a tally on each wire. Its own legend says the wires are not routes, and its own summary says no drawn wire has a law of change.
reports.why_not_good_enough:
Asked for: a map of dynamics. Its features are the conditions something can be in and the passages between them. The project's own words say so: AGENTS.md, "an attractor, transition or correspondence mapped"; WHOLE-PICTURE.md, "Places as nodes, changes as arrows".

Built: a schema of the laws' sentence parts (kinds of role, kinds of tie) with a coverage tally laid on it. Its subject is the corpus of theorems, not what the theorems describe. A node is a noun, an edge is a verb drawn subject to object, position is set by hand, line weight is a count of catalogue entries. Nothing on it is a state, so nothing can move: the atlas's 103 transitions and 321 exits became counts under "begins", "ends" and "where the line falls", and the page then reports no law of change on any tie.

Asked for: a map of how things form, last, change and end (what a selection reaches, drains and locks on; where each course leads and under what condition; who bears it), drawn first for alignment and also of wisdom, so a person can see the way.

Built: a typed index of the account's own stock. Its nodes are grammatical roles, not conditions a thing can be in. Its arrows are kinds of relation, not changes ("an arrow is not a route"). Its measures are counts of laws and tests per arrow. At that grain the dynamics cannot appear: 80 of 183 fall on one arrow, a drain and a renewal carry the same three ties, and the atlas's eight family names occur nowhere. The purpose cannot appear either: alignment, meta-attractor, instrumental convergence, 生生, ethics and tradition are absent from the first page, and the meta-attractor's own entries sit in the residual bin because they have no law.

What the page reports as "what the map shows today" is the fill-rate of its filing scheme, a scheme its own foundation note found fits 86 of 462 laws. So it tells a reader what the account lacks instead of what it sees. It is the map-makers' ledger, shown as the map.

reports.a_good_one_would: Without choosing anything, a person sees a terrain of what happens. Something goes on through what gives back to it. Many draw, overshoot, pass a point of no return, end. A selection reads only what couples into it and drains what lies beyond. A rule read from its own winners locks; winners shape the rule; the readers of the loss are drawn out; the closed loop is named the meta-attractor. From each lock the ways out are drawn, each path carrying its condition (a reading of what lies beyond the share, before the point of no return). Renewal and 生生 are regimes on the same ground, not a separate good zone. Each place has one everyday sentence, a familiar example, and the names others gave it (Goodhart, Stigler, 黄宗羲, Plato's cave). reports.against_ren:
1. He approved each step ("Yes, build on it", "Yes, land it"), and his round-2 requests taken alone (logic apart from situation; words not only for persons; one map) specify nearly what was built. "This map can guide us to understand the relationships between reasoning and the actual data" describes an instrument for the makers, and that is what landed. The fault is that it replaced the round-1 request (a map of what happens, for a stranger) instead of being laid on it as a layer. His two wants pull apart unless layered; "not good enough" is not only an execution failure.

2. "A map, not a set of maps" was read as one picture at one grain. If he means that literally, I think it is wrong for 183 dynamics: one territory at several scales is still one map, and the coarsest grain alone shows no dynamics.

3. "Heavily dualistic" was answered by removing every name of what happens (drain, capture, lock, stagnation, renewal: 0 family names on the map). If he meant the names, I disagree: AGENTS.md itself names what we want to stay out of and says "Say it plainly". Non-dual here is drawing lock and release as two regimes of one tie with the condition between them, which the atlas's exits hold and the map dropped.

4. Where the map is right: its test numbers are true and belong somewhere; the meta-attractor's upper orders really have no law ("A working definition, with no law yet"). A good map must draw that as argued or a reading, a visible hole, not file it under the legend.

reports.say_back: A reader learns how the account is shelved: eleven kinds of role, the ties between them, and how many laws and tests sit on each. Looking long, they may see that a stock stands in the middle and that only "reaches, or lies beyond" joins it to a rule. They learn that proofs and tests are kept apart, and that 26 predictions agreed where every condition was met and none disagreed. They do not learn what happens to anything: the first page has 419 numbers and no sentence of a course. One click deeper it is better than the diagnosis allows: each of the 183 dynamics has one plain sentence, a chosen dynamic lights its own figure, a chosen test shows what was taken as which role. So the reader meets a sound store and its shelf plan, under the title "The map".

reports.a_good_one_would: The reader opens one picture and can say back what the account sees: a few named figures on the one web (living on a stock; a rule that locks; a reading and what it is of), each with one sentence and one example from the world. Opening the lock shows its six dynamics in order: what leads in, what holds, what grows meanwhile unread, what leads out. Each arrow is marked as proved, one built example, needing a change from outside, or a reading, and holes are drawn as holes. On the same figure the reader lays a situation (a test, a tradition's saying, their own): which thing is which role, which answers place it, what the reasoning then says, and what in that pairing is unchecked or has failed. What reaches a rule and what lies beyond it is the first thing seen. Counts sit a layer below.
reports.against_ren:
1. "a map, not a set of maps", taken as one picture, is what pushed the ground up to eleven abstract kinds and cost the readable layer. Beside his own "layered, indexed ... entry points" it has to mean one ground seen at several depths. I would argue that with him before building again.
2. On one narrow point the map is right against "even when one is right, the other could be wrong": a theorem on its stated model is not made wrong by a case. It is wrong only in stopping there, since the pairing and the thesis are reasoning too.
3. A truthful map of states and routes will be thin: 70 of 321 exits name another dynamic, 160 are single built examples, six joins are proved. If "not good enough" includes wanting a connected whole, part of that is the account's present state and not its drawing. The rest can be joined only as readings said as readings, which AGENTS.md allows ("argued, a reading, or wanted").
4. His "Yes, land it" answered "Is this the one map you meant?" on the first build, before two reviews changed it. It confirms one ground. It does not say the page reads well, so the two answers do not conflict.
5. Against the coordinator, not Ren: going back to round 1's boxes alone would undo what he ranked higher. DESIGN.md already settled that a place is a name for a set of answers on the web, not a rival structure.
